extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, IP professionals, and stakeholders interested in Chinese patent practice
extracted.subtask_short: inventiveness exam for Chinese utility models
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes CNIPA's amended Patent Examination Guidelines (effective Jan 20, 2024) with emphasis on the newly-described preliminary examination of utility models for obvious lack of novelty and inventiveness and the substantive principles for judging inventiveness of utility models vs. invention patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary examination — obvious lack of novelty and inventiveness (Article 22 ¶2 & ¶3)
rubrics_metrics.description: During the preliminary examination, the examiner will examine whether the utility model patent application obviously lacks novelty and inventiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner can examine whether the utility model patent application obviously lacks novelty based on the information he obtains about the prior art or conflicting applications. For examination on novelty, refer to Chapter 3 of Part II and Chapter 6, Section 3 of Part IV of the Guidelines. The examiner can examine whether a utility model patent application obviously lacks inventive step based on the information he or she has obtained about the prior art; for inventive step, refer to Section 4 of Chapter 6 of Part 4 of the Guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of all technical features in inventiveness review
rubrics_metrics.description: In the examination of the inventiveness of a utility model patent, all technical features of the technical solution, including material features and method features, should be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the relevant contents of the inventiveness examination of utility model patents — including concept of inventiveness, examination principles, examination criteria and judgment of inventiveness of different types of inventions — refer to provisions of Chapter 4 of Part II of the Guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of creativity/inventiveness for utility models vs invention patents
rubrics_metrics.description: The standard of creativity (inventiveness) for utility model patents should be lower than that for invention patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: According to Article 22 ¶3, creativity means the invention has 'outstanding substantive features and significant progress compared with the existing technology.' The Guidelines state the difference between invention patents and utility models in inventiveness judgment is mainly reflected in whether there is 'technical inspiration' in the existing technology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field of existing technology to consider when judging inventiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Scope of prior-art fields considered differs between invention patents and utility models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For invention patents: consider not only the technical field to which the invention belongs, but also similar or related technical fields and technical problems that could prompt skilled persons to search in other fields. For utility model patents: generally focus on the technical field to which the utility model belongs; however, if the prior art provides clear inspiration (e.g., records prompting skilled persons to search related fields), similar or related technical fields may be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantity of prior art to cite for inventiveness evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of prior-art references used to evaluate inventiveness differs by patent type and circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For invention patents: one, two or more prior art can be cited to evaluate creativity. For utility model patents: one or two prior art can generally be cited to evaluate inventiveness. For utility models formed by 'simple superposition' of existing technologies, multiple prior art can be cited depending on the situation and assessed accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to detailed provisions in the Guidelines for procedure and substantive examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Guidelines provide procedural and substantive examination guidance analogous to the USPTO MPEP and identify where detailed rules for novelty and inventive step are located.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novelty: see Chapter 3 of Part II and Chapter 6, Section 3 of Part IV. Inventive step (utility models): see Section 4 of Chapter 6 of Part 4 and Chapter 4 of Part II for detailed concepts, principles, criteria and judgment approaches.
